117731.name: Chabad Lubavitch Center Regional Hdqts.
117731.note: Lubavitch.com, 11 March 2003 ('A 30th B-day for Chabad of the Lone Star State'): Chabad Lubavitch of Texas 'celebrated 30 years in the state' on 9 March 2003; 'in 1972, when Rabbi Shimon and Chiena Lazaroff ... came to Houston'. The Jewish Herald-Voice's 2022 section on Chabad's 50 years in Texas (ChabadInfo, 'Chabad's 50-year Lone Star Journey'): 'When the Lazaroffs first arrived in Houston on May 10, 1972'; construction of the center on Fondren Road (the first Chabad center built from the ground up) began in 1977 and it opened for the High Holy Days in 1978 (CrownHeights.info, Jan 2007, says the center was founded in 1976); before that, an apartment.

117728.name: Chabad of Dallas
117728.note: Its own About page: 'In 1984, Rabbi Mendel and Baila Dubrawsky were inspired by the Rebbe's vision' and settled in Dallas, starting with small classes, Shabbat meals and holiday celebrations. The Jewish Herald-Voice's 2022 history (ChabadInfo) agrees: 'In 1984, Rabbi Mendel and Baila Dubrawsky went to Dallas.' Against: COLlive (May 2021) has them arriving in 1985.

117727.name: Chabad of Austin
117727.note: Chabad of Texas's 50-year history (Jewish Herald-Voice, 2022, on ChabadInfo): 'In 1980, Rabbi Traxler and his wife, Shoshana, were appointed as shluchim of Chabad in Austin' (Rabbi Moishe Traxler had been one of the first UT students involved with Chabad, from 1972). The Jewish Outlook (Shalom Austin, June 2024, 'Journey of Growth'): the story of Chabad in Austin began in 1973 with Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff's trips from Houston to teach UT students; 'Nearly a decade later, Rabbi Yosef Levertov moved to Austin at the invitation of the then UT rabbi, Rabbi Traxler'; 'In 1984, Rabbi Yosef Levertov and his wife Rochel Levertov moved to Austin to join Chabad Lubavitch of Austin and two years later they were given the keys.' So the center was there before the Levertovs: its own About page dates its journey from their arrival in 1984 ('Our journey in Austin commenced in 1984'). The Traxlers then moved to Houston (Chabad Outreach of Houston).

117926.name: Chabad of Plano/Collin County
117926.note: Its own About page: 'Chabad of Plano founded in 1992'; 'over the past 30 years, Chabad of Plano has grown'; its gallery has a '2022 Event - Celebrating 30 Years'. (Lubavitch.com, March 2003, lists Plano among the centers established from Houston.)

118556.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Fort Worth & Tarrant County
118556.note: Its own home page: 'In September of 2002, Chabad Headquarters in Texas' appointed Rabbi Dov and Chana Tovah Mandel directors of Chabad activities in Tarrant County. Lubavitch.com (March 2003) already lists Fort Worth among the centers established from Houston.

2456591.name: Chabad of Frisco
2456591.note: The Frisco Enterprise (CrownHeights.info, 17 Sept 2015): Rabbi Mendy and Mushkie Kesselman 'moved from New York to Frisco ... in August 2014'. COLlive (18 Nov 2014, after Chabad.org): they 'moved to Texas to build their own Chabad community in the town of Frisco' (Mushkie is the daughter of Plano's Rabbi Menachem and Rivka Block).

4026720.name: Chabad of Cypress
4026720.note: COLlive, 30 Aug 2018 (after Chabad.org, 27 Aug 2018, 'Hurricane Harvey Anniversary Gift: A New Chabad Center'): 'The 12th Chabad center in the Houston area, to be co-directed by Rabbi Levi and Devorah Leah Marinovsky, was timed to start by the anniversary of Hurricane Harvey'.

4476658.name: Chabad of Allen-McKinney
4476658.note: Lubavitch.com, 4 Oct 2019 ('Fiftieth Chabad in the Lone Star State'): 'In October, Rabbi Sholom and Chaya Block will be ... setting out to serve the Jewish communities in Allen and McKinney, Texas', the fiftieth Chabad couple in Texas. Today Rabbi Eli and Nechama Newman run Chabad of Allen-McKinney (ChabadAM.org); the chabad.org listing (4476658) is from about 2019. That the Newmans took over the Blocks' center isn't stated anywhere found: medium.

5381032.name: Chabad of Boerne
5381032.note: Lubavitch.com (CrownHeights.info, 23 Aug 2023): 'in Boerne, Texas, a fledgling Chabad center is led by Rabbi Yossi and Malkie Marrus', with Chabad of San Antonio since 1997; 'in 2021 they left San Antonio's ... winding roads for the longhorn cattle ranches of Boerne'.

5587788.name: Chabad of Leander
5587788.note: Lubavitch.com (CrownHeights.info, 23 Dec 2024, 'Chabad Opens in Leander, Texas, Amid Tech-Fueled Boom'): a family that moved to Leander in 2021 heard, 'two years after moving to town', of its first-ever public menorah lighting, 'held by Rabbi Shmuly and Nechomele Levertov, who'd just moved to town to found Chabad of Leander' (so about 2023). The year is worked out, not stated: medium.

6262181.name: Chabad of Carrollton-Lewisville
6262181.note: COLlive, 17 Sept 2024: 'For the past 18 years, Rabbi Yudi and Esther Horowitz have been on Shlichus in Plano, Texas. Now, they are heading out to establish Chabad of Carrollton-Lewisville in North Texas', with the approval of Rabbi Mendel Dubrawsky.

118570.name: Chabad of Sugar Land
118570.note: COLlive, 6 Sept 2010: 'On Sunday, August 29, Chabad of Sugar Land, Texas, led by Rabbi Mendel and Chaya Feigenson, celebrated their 10th anniversary at their annual dinner' (count back: 2000). Its site calls the Feigensons its 'Founding Rabbi and Directors'. An anniversary count: medium.

1392216.name: The Shul of Bellaire
1392216.note: Chabad.org, 6 April 2016 ('Bellaire, Texas: A Magnet for Jewish Families in Southwest Houston'): Rabbi Yossi Zaklikofsky says the family moved to Bellaire at the end of 2010; the 2016 gala marked 'Five years of Jewish growth at The Shul of Bellaire' (the shul from about 2011). Before that they were appointed to Pearland (CrownHeights.info, 8 Dec 2008: to 'establish a new Chabad House serving ... Alvin, Friendswood and Pearland').

1324719.name: Chabad of The Woodlands
1324719.note: Chabad.org, 2 Sept 2013 ('Big Cattle, Big Hats and a Bigger Chabad Center'): Rabbi Mendel and Leah Blecher 'came to the community in 2011', working out of their home at first. CrownHeights.info (5 Feb 2014) agrees: the growth 'since he founded Chabad of The Woodlands three years ago'.

397245.name: Chabad of the Rio Grande Valley
397245.note: CrownHeights.info, 17 May 2010: 'Rabbi Asher and Dini Hecht ... have recently moved on Shlichus to the Rio Grande Valley of Texas where they will be establishing a new Chabad center', appointed by Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff. But chabad.org already listed Chabad of the Rio Grande Valley (397245, a listing from about 2005) beside a July 2007 report on Camp Gan Israel on South Padre Island, so there was something under that name before the Hechts: medium.

1090905.name: Camp Gan Israel South Padre Island Texas
1090905.note: Chabad.org, 11 July 2007 ('A Splashing Success'): campers at 'the Chabad-Lubavitch Camp Gan Israel on South Padre Island' spent 'sixteen action-packed days on the island'; 'The camp welcomed kids from across the dry expanse of Texas.' So running by summer 2007; its first year not stated. Today Rabbi Asher Hecht (Rio Grande Valley) is its director.

117919.name: Chabad at Texas Medical Center
117919.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 31 Aug 2011, 'Houston Patients Find a Caring Embrace in Aishel House'): 'The Lazaroffs launched what would eventually become the Aishel House in 1992, not long after moving to the area around the medical center' (Rabbi Eliezer and Rochel Lazaroff); in 1995 they added a two-bedroom apartment as its first hospitality department, and in 2003 the center bought an adjacent 18-unit apartment building.

earlier.where: a two-bedroom apartment beside the Medical Center (its first hospitality department)

512666.name: Rohr Chabad Jewish Center at Texas A&M University
512666.note: CrownHeights.info, 30 April 2007 ('New Shluchim to Texas'): 'Rabbi Yossi and Manya Lazaroff will IYH be moving on Shlichus to College Station, Texas where they will establish a new Chabad House serving the students and faculty at Texas A&M University', appointed by Chabad of Texas. Chabad.org's news on it starts in July 2007.

536472.name: The Igor Tulchinsky Chabad Campus at the University of Texas at Austin
536472.note: The Jewish Outlook (CrownHeights.info, 6 Aug 2007): 'Rabbi Zev Johnson and his wife, Ariela, are co-directing Chabad House, Rabbi Yosef and Rochel Levertov announced. The Johnsons arrived in June' to manage Chabad's campus activities at the University of Texas. The year is the campus center's own directors'; Chabad at UT itself goes back to the Levertovs (1984, Chabad of Austin) and Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff's first meetings with UT students (1972).

117732.name: Chabad Center for Jewish Life & Learning
117732.note: The Jewish Herald-Voice's 2022 history of Chabad in Texas (ChabadInfo, 'Chabad's 50-year Lone Star Journey'): after the Dubrawskys went to Dallas in 1984, 'The next year, Rabbi Chaim and Rivkie Block opened in San Antonio.' Other accounts agree the center was founded in 1985 by Rabbi Chaim and Rivkie Block and moved in 1987 to a larger site in the North Central area.

117729.name: Chabad Lubavitch
117729.note: The Jewish Herald-Voice's 2022 history of Chabad in Texas (ChabadInfo): 'In 1986, Chabad El Paso was established with Rabbi Yisroel and Chana Greenberg appointed as directors.' CrownHeights.info (2011, 'After 25 Years, Next Generation Serves at Synagogue') and others put the Greenbergs' arrival in 1986 too.

4816645.name: Chabad Israeli Center
4816645.note: The Jewish Herald-Voice's 2022 history of Chabad in Texas (ChabadInfo): 'Houston opening its latest Chabad House in 2020 – the Israeli Center, serving Hebrew-speaking and Israeli families of Houston' (Rabbi Mendel Raichik). The chabad.org listing (4816645) is from about 2020.

6293873.name: Chabad of Lubbock at Texas Tech University
6293873.note: Lubavitch.com, 21 Nov 2024 ('Lubbock, Texas Welcomes Chabad Presence'): 'Rabbi Zalman and Chana Liba Braun moved to Lubbock earlier this year, to serve the needs of Jewish students at Texas Tech as well as the local Jewish community'; Lubbock had been 'the largest remaining U.S. city without a Chabad presence'. (Their first visits, with Chanukah menorah lightings, came before the move.)

4814414.name: Chabad of Texas Towns
4814414.note: COLlive, 16 Feb 2021 (after Chabad.org, 15 Feb 2021, 'Chabad on the Range Serving Jews in Rural Texas'): 'Rabbi Saadya and Chaya Sara Kaufmann ... have established Chabad of Texas Towns', launched during the coronavirus pandemic; 'In the fall, the Kaufmanns organized a Sukkah mobile ... and on Chanukah, they held the first-ever public menorah-lighting in Beaumont' (fall 2020). They live in Houston.

4158975.name: Chabad of Richardson and UTD
4158975.note: Its own About page: 'Chabad of Richardson and UTD was established in 2021' (Rabbi Shmuly and Dini Druk). The chabad.org listing (4158975) is older, about 2018-19.

6522358.name: Chabad of the Park Cities
6522358.note: Its own About page: 'Chabad of the Park Cities was founded in 2024'; Rabbi Baruch and Mooka Hecht 'moved to University Park in spring 2024' to start the area's first Jewish community (he came to Dallas nearly a decade earlier as co-rabbi of The Intown Chabad).

674341.name: Chabad of Southlake
674341.note: Its own About page: 'Founded in 2008, Chabad of Southlake (Arlington) is a hub of Jewish spirituality and social activities' (Rabbi Levi and Rishi Gurevitch). The chabad.org listing (674341) is from about 2008 too.

4866998.name: Chabad of Rockwall County
4866998.note: Its own 'Meet Us' page: 'Rabbi Moishy and Chana moved to Rockwall, Texas in 2020, with their 2 daughters, Musya and Leah, to start a Chabad House' (the Kalmensons).

4174253.name: Chabad of Roundrock
4174253.note: Its own About page (Jewish Round Rock): 'We have been living in Round Rock since April of 2019' (Rabbi Mendel and Mussi Marasow); the Jewish Outlook (Shalom Austin, June 2024, 'Journey of Growth'): 'Chabad of Round Rock was formed in 2019 and is led by Rabbi Mendel and Mussi Marasow'. Two sources agree. (Its site's footer reads '© 2018-2026 Jewish Round Rock', and the chabad.org listing (4174253) is from about 2018-19.)

758578.name: Chabad of West Houston
758578.note: Its own site: 'Chabad of West Houston, Inc., began its programing with High Holiday Services and other educational programs, in rented space at the JCC of West Houston, in September of 2005' (Rabbi Dovid and Elisa Goldstein, in Houston as emissaries since 1998, first with Rabbi Traxler's Chabad Outreach).

earlier.where: rented space at the JCC of West Houston

356368.name: Chabad of Uptown
356368.note: Jewish Herald-Voice (via CrownHeights.info): 'Rabbi Chaim and Chanie Lazaroff began serving the Houston community in 2002, establishing Chabad Uptown in February 2006.' Chabad.org (June 2008): Chabad of Uptown 'just moved into temporary quarters after outgrowing its previous home'.

1595101.name: Chabad of the Bay Area
1595101.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, May 2014, 'No Torahs on Mars Yet, but One Small Step Closer'), and The Galveston County Daily News ('Jewish center opens in League City'): Rabbi Yitzchok and Malky Schmukler came in the summer of 2012 to start Chabad of the Bay Area for the Jews of Clear Lake, Pearland and Galveston.

157731.name: Chabad at Rice University
157731.note: Its own 'Meet the Slonim Family' page: Rabbi Shmuli (Shmuel) and Nechama Slonim 'moved to Houston in May of 2016 to establish Chabad on Campus for Jewish students in Houston' (Rice, the University of Houston and the medical schools); it was at 1950 Dryden Road before the new Grinshtein center (1915 University Blvd., ground broken 2026). But the chabad.org listing (157731) is far older (about 2004), so a Chabad at Rice existed before them, perhaps the Medical Center's: medium.

5112185.name: Cheder Lubavitch of Dallas
5112185.note: COLlive, 25 May 2021: Rabbi Aharon Simon is moving to Texas 'to serve as the principal of the new Chabad Cheder' in the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex; COLlive, 22 Dec 2021: 'A newly opened Chabad Cheder in Dallas, Texas ... is providing a warm, Chasidishe Chinuch to 25 children.' (Today Rabbi Moshe Naparstek is listed.)

1279173.name: The Intown Chabad
1279173.note: Chabad.org, 5 Oct 2026 ('In Dallas, Hundreds of Young Jews Fill Synagogue Over Holiday Season'): its history 'dates back to the early 2000s', with Rabbi Mendel Dubrawsky's weekly class for singles in Uptown; 'When the Drizins, Dubrawsky's daughter and son-in-law, arrived in Dallas as emissaries in 2004', they 'began providing more programming to the young professionals', 'moved there three years later, and so The Intown Chabad was born' (2007). Its charity listing says founded in 2007.

3486373.name: Chabad Jewish Center of San Marcos Texas
3486373.note: Shalom Austin (Jewish Outlook, Feb 2025, 'San Marcos Jewish Community Is Flourishing'): 'Even before Chabad of San Marcos was officially established, Rabbi Weingarten was already actively working with Jewish students at Texas State University', setting up a new Jewish student group at the students' request in 2015; 'The Rohr Chabad of San Marcos opened its doors in 2016'. The year is that first activity; the center opened in 2016.

4887459.name: Chabad of South Austin
4887459.note: Anash.org, 29 Oct 2020 ('New Shluchim to America's Fastest-Growing City'): 'America's fastest-growing city will soon be getting a new Chabad center with the appointment of Rabbi Mendel and Rikki Hertz as the new shluchim to South Austin, Texas', under Rabbi Yosef Levertov, still raising seed money. Shalom Austin (2024): by 2021 another Chabad was needed south of the river. The year is the appointment; the first programs may have come in 2021: medium.

3872731.name: Chabad Israeli Center
3872731.note: Cause IQ, from IRS data: Chabad Israeli Center San Antonio (15511 Oak Grove Drive; EIN 84-1947648), year formed 2019. An IRS record bounds it ('by'); its start not found. The chabad.org listing (3872731) is from about 2017.

5215392.name: Maayan Chai
5215392.note: Texas Jewish Post, 1 April 2010 (p. 8, on The Portal to Texas History): Maayan Chai, a nonprofit offering Jewish learning, business networking and one-on-one advice, launched by Gavin Kam with Dan (now Rabbi) Lewin, who had hosted Sinai Cafe and studied at the Mayanot yeshiva in Jerusalem. So there by April 2010; its exact start not read (the page was unavailable).
